Detusche Interview Experience
Graduate Analyst 2024
Sachit A. Sankhe
Final Year B.Tech IT 2020-24
Eligibility:-
●CS, IT, EXTC only
●7+ CPI
About the FTE offer:-
●19.63 LPA
●Pune/Bangalore location
About the company:-
Deutsche Bank has its most banking customers in Europe with it being founded in
Germany. Deutsche Bank is a global financial institution that offers a wide range of
banking and financial services to individuals, businesses, and institutions worldwide.
(Once check the pronunciation of Detusche especially if you are going for the interview).

Deutsche hired for the Graduate Analyst role in the Technology and Data Innovation
Department.
The entire process includes 1 online coding test and 4 rounds of interviews.
(Technical Round 1, Technical Round 2, Professional Fit round, HR round)
Online test:-
The test was scheduled for 4th August on Hackerearth. It was a standard
DSA-based online coding test. Test Duration was 1hr 30 min and the test had 3
questions.
Q1) Power generation
The problem had a story behind it. But what we had to do was calculate the
maximum time required for draining 2 power sources.
Now the way this power drains is that if we are currently using say power source
A, then its power reduces by 2 units, and the power of the other power source
(currently not in use) increases by 1. And we have to stop whenever at least 1
source reaches zero.
Eg. We have source A = 3 and B = 5
→So at t=0 we choose B and hence at
T = 1, A = 4, B = 3
T = 2, A = 5, B = 1
T = 3, A = 3, B = 2
T = 4, A = 1, B = 3

T = 5, A = 2, B = 1
T = 6, A = 0, B = 2
Here since A reached zero, we stop and the ans is 6.
Solution:-
I solved it using DP. Some of my friends also solved it iteratively using a while
loop. The iterative is also very intuitive. Just maintain 2 variables that contain
max and min amongst the two sources and then while none of them are less
than or equal to zero, reduce the max values amongst them by 2, increase the
min value by 1, and then again update the values of the max and min variable.
This was an easy-medium problem. There is also a score associated with these
questions. This one had 20 points.
Q2 ) Auto suggestions
This was a variation of the famous EDIT DISTANCE problem (solved using
DP). This question did not require memoization, because I wrote the
recursive solution and submitted and it got accepted.
There was an array of strings and a query string given, you had to find the
word closest to the given query string.
There are 2 factors to decide the closeness of a word with the query string:
1) Levenshtein distance:- Minimum number of operations to convert a
given string to the query string. Operations allowed are
a) Insertion

b) Deletion
c) Updation
2) If 2 strings have the same Levenshtein distance then the string that is
lexicographically smallest will be the closest to the query string.
Solution:-
Iterate over all the strings in the array. And then calculate the Levenshtein
distance(using the edit distance method). Then if 2 strings have the same
minimum Levenshtein distance, then choose the lexicographically smaller
string.
It was a medium problem.
Q3) Sorting related something
I don't exactly remember the story in the question, but there were 2 arrays
given, one was a string array and the second was an int array. You had to
sort the string array in descending order using the corresponding values
from the int array. And if 2 strings have the same corresponding value in the
int array then preserve the natural ordering.
Eg. str = [“abc”, “def”, “ghi”], value = [12,12,48]
So, the final answer output array will be [“ghi”, ”abc”, ”def”].
Since “abc” and “def” both have the same value, hence maintain the same
order as given in the original array.
Solution:- You had to write a custom comparator for sorting these string
arrays (in Java). In C++ there must be another way to write a custom sorter.

Make a pair of strings and their corresponding values and then sort this
new array and then create a new array for storing the strings from the
sorted array.
This was an easy-medium problem if you knew how to write a custom
sorter.
Note:- The HackerEarth editor had a lot of problems with the Java
language. For C++ there were no problems. So be aware and check the
input provided to your function if you use Java.
I lost a lot of time due to these problems. However, I was able to solve all
the problems with 15 minutes left for the test to end.
The results were announced on 7th August and we had our offline
interviews on 9th August from 9:00 am.
Round 1 of Interview:-
The interviews started at around 9:30 am and my interview started around
10:00 am.
I was first asked to introduce myself. (The only question you can be sure of
when preparing).
The introduction is one of the most important pieces of preparation as you
can easily steer the interview into the zone where you are confident and can
leave a good impression on the interviewer.

The interviewer asked a few general questions on my introduction. Then
the interviewer started asking general computer science questions. The
questions included
1) Storage sizes( bytes, Kb, Mb etc.)
2) Private and Public IP
3) What is polymorphism and its types
4) Diff between broadcast, multicast, and unicast.
5) DSA question
The question was that you have been given a Circular linked list and you
have to break it down into 2 equal-length circular linked lists.
6) What are your personal projects about?
7) Did you use git for your projects tell me about git commands.
There were also some HR questions such as “Tell me about your strengths
and weaknesses”. And whether you want to pursue future education.
There were many small questions asked throughout the interview.
According to me, this interview was just to gauge whether a candidate has
a basic understanding of all the core subjects or not.
The interview lasted for about 45 to 50 minutes. Around 30 people were
shortlisted for the next round.

Round 2 of Interview:
My second round started around 12:15 pm and this was a 1hr 30 to
45 minute interview. This was a proper technical interview.
The interviewer went through my resume at the beginning and questioned
me about the details mentioned in the resume.
Then the interviewer asked questions about my internships and why I chose
some frameworks or language to perform certain tasks during my
internship and my projects.
Then the interviewer asked me to rate myself in DSA from 0 to 5. I said 3.
Then the interviewer asked me the difference between Data Structures and
Algorithms. And then asked some basic questions about diff between trees
and graphs. And then the interviewer gave me a problem. I don’t remember
the question but it was straightforward BFS. However, the interviewer asked
me to write the complete code on paper. The interviewer expected me to
write everything starting from the Node class to the final output function.
Then she also asked me to do the problem using DFS, this time interviewer
just asked me to write pseudo code.
After this, the interviewer asked me Segregate 0s and 1s in an array -
GeeksforGeeks problem. Deutsche always asks some or the other version
of Sort an array of 0s, 1s and 2s | Dutch National Flag problem -
GeeksforGeeks.

After this, there were some questions on Dynamic programming and she
just asked me to explain the benefit of using DP for calculating factorial.
Just the pseudo-code for this problem.
After this, the interviewer asked me a puzzle Riddle of the Week #6: The
Burning Rope Problem (popularmechanics.com). I was not able to solve the
puzzle but the interviewer explained the solution at the end.
TIPS:- Whenever you find a problem that is given to you, always keep on
talking about your thought process and also what is the blocker in your
approach. Also always discuss the TC and SC for all the problems. I was
asked to do the same for all the problems.
Round 3 of Interview:-
The third round was the Professional Fit Round. The interviewer asked me
the following questions:
1) Introduce yourself and I was questioned based on my introduction.
2) Next, the interviewer gave a scenario where I am the developer who is
going to talk with the client about a certain project. The interviewer
gave me a certain description of the project. And then asked me what
questions I would ask the client to get the low-level requirements. (I
answered I would ask the client how many customers could be using
the product and also what type of data that would be involved etc.)
3) Now the product is developed and is in production and a bug has
occurred, what will be my actions ahead? (I answered firstly I would

take a look at the code and try and examine the fault. And then
also reassure the client that it will be fixed ASAP etc.)
4) Now let’s say the bug occurred only and only because of a
requirement that the customer had not told you before and now the
client is angry and shouting at you. (I replied that I would first go
through the requirements I was told during the first meeting and also
evaluate what was my interpretation of requirements and
simultaneously what the client meant by those requirements etc.)
5) Now you have been given some work by your manager in a tech stack
that is new to you. And you will be provided enough training regarding
the tech stack but you are not liking this work. What will you do( I
replied that I will first talk with my manager and inform him about my
situation and then discuss if it is possible to revalute the resource
allocation for the project and maybe can I get some other work.but if
the work is on top priority then I will give my best and complete the
work and then discuss with the manager what is to be done
afterward)
6) Now the situation is that you are given a new tech stack and you are
ok with the work, but the time left to deliver the project is very less
and hence you cannot be provided with the formal training, so you
just have one week to start working on the project but there are some
team members who are expert in this stack, but the catch is that you
are not in good relations with those team members. ( I replied that
the project should be my focus and I should be professional in such
conditions and seek help from the team members, If they are still not
being professional in these conditions then I should take it that I have
to deliver the best that I can on my own and once the projects

deadline is completed I can take these things up with the manager
for discussion).
7) At last, there was a brief discussion about the policy of Deutsche
Bank for such scenarios and also about their recent partnership with
the Google Cloud Program and data security laws in Europe.
The interview lasted about 50 min to 1 hr.
Round 4 of interview:-
I was called for the 4th round within 15 minutes of my 3rd round
completion. Do read upon the values of Deutsche Bank. This was a HR
round with the HR managers from Deutsche Bank
1) Introduce yourself
2) Then I was asked about my internships and what I learned from my
internships
3) Then I was asked to think of a scenario where I did some task in a
certain way and then I realized after doing it, that this approach has
reached a blocker which will take a lot of time to solve and even after
spending the time you are not sure that it would be solved, how will
you tackle such scenarios (Luckily I had faced such a condition in my
internship so I told about the scenario).
4) A scenario where the team did not agree with my point of view.
5) The interviewer asked whether I was a team player or a solo leader.
6) The values of Deutsche Bank
7) What are your future study plans?
8) Where do you see yourself in 5 years?

9) Why Deutsche Bank? ( I replied that I have spoken with my seniors
who are working in DB, and they had good reviews about the work
environment and culture and I am also personally interested in the
finance domain)
There were some more standard HR questions asked during the interview.
It was only about 15 to 20 min.
I was done with all of my 4 rounds by 5 p.m.
The wait for the result for very long but worth it, The result were announced
at around 8 pm and I was among the selected candidates.
